subject.title: Subagent Premature Announce Bug - Model-Specific Tool Call Handling Issues

question: Should OpenClaw execute provider-specific tagged tool-call markers when they appear inside thinking content for Qwen/ModelStudio-style models?
rationale: Source inspection shows the remaining gap, but deciding whether reasoning text can become executable tool calls is a security and product boundary rather than a mechanical parser choice.

options.title: Conservative provider-owned promotion
options.body: Approve a Qwen/ModelStudio-scoped parser that only promotes standalone tagged sections after allowed-tool validation and live provider proof.

options.title: Keep thinking non-executable
options.body: Treat thinking-only tagged markers as unsupported provider output and document that users should choose a model or endpoint that emits structured tool calls.

options.title: Broader shared repair
options.body: Expand shared tool-call repair to scan thinking payloads across providers, accepting a larger security and regression surface.

recommendation.title: Conservative provider-owned promotion
recommendation.body: Approve a Qwen/ModelStudio-scoped parser that only promotes standalone tagged sections after allowed-tool validation and live provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans provider support, OpenAI-compatible transport behavior, and adjacent tool-call safety work where steipete has the broadest recent history.
